result.title: Where Mixture Recognition Fails: An Ingredient-Level Audit of Unseen Combinations in SmellNet
result.summary: An electronic nose must name every ingredient of a mixture, including combinations it has never measured. SmellNet, a public benchmark for this task, scores ingredients with a hit rate that is told how many each sample contains. We audit what this protocol hides. We hold out ingredient combinations from the SmellNet training data, evaluate four architectures (MLP, CNN, LSTM and a Transformer encoder) without revealing the ingredient count, and repeat the evaluation once on the official unseen split. Under the count-informed protocol, 90-96% of mixtures receive an ingredient that is absent, on our folds and on the official split alike. On our folds, every model identifies one ingredient reliably but the second rarely, and it completes the pair with a familiar training partner about twice as often as chance. On the official split, even the first-ranked ingredient is correct in only 29-46% of binary mixtures, often because a frequent training ingredient that is absent from every test pair is ranked first, and on its combinations that are truly absent from training no model names both ingredients in more than 1.2% of them. The failures fall on the same ingredients for every architecture, and a frequency correction only moves errors between ingredients. Mixture recognition is therefore limited by ingredients the models cannot separate and by a preference for frequent ingredients, not by the architecture, and it should be evaluated with set-level errors and without oracle cardinality.

AI.brief_summary: 论文审计电子鼻混合物识别基准 SmellNet：留出未见成分组合、在不告知成分数的条件下评测四种架构，并复核官方 unseen split，发现失败集中在模型无法分离的成分与高频成分偏好上，而非架构本身。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属化学传感而非视觉，但其「去除 oracle 成分数先验、改用集合级错误」的评测口径与逐成分失败归因，可能为 LVR 中步骤数/停止决策先验和集合式输出评测提供可核查的思路。
